notes: **Cho tôi … is the only sentence you need to order anything.** Literally "give me …", and although it sounds like a command in translation, in Vietnamese it's the most natural and polite form at stalls, shops and cafés. The full pattern is exactly the one from Unit 4: *cho tôi* + number + classifier + noun.

**Hay and hoặc both mean "or", but they can't be swapped.** *Hay* is used in **questions** — *phở tái **hay** phở chín?* *Hoặc* is used in **statements** — *tôi uống cà phê **hoặc** trà* (I drink coffee or tea). English uses one word for both, so this is a genuinely new distinction you have to practice.

**Tự means "oneself" and goes before the verb**: *tự cho* (help yourself), *tự làm* (do it yourself), *tự học* (self-study). On a Vietnamese stall table there's almost always a tray of chili, lime, bean sprouts and herbs — all *tự*, and never charged extra.

**Trà đá is the drink you'll meet most often**, and at many stalls it's **free** — the iced-tea jug sits on the table and you refill it yourself. Don't be puzzled if it isn't on the bill; that's no oversight.

**No means "full" and đói means "hungry"**, and both are adjectives, so they stand alone with no verb: *Tôi no rồi.* (I'm full), *Tôi đói quá!* (I'm starving!). The question *Ăn no chưa?* isn't empty small talk — the owner really will offer more if you say not yet.

**Giúp tôi means "help me" and goes AFTER the verb**: *tính tiền **giúp tôi*** (could you add up the bill), *gọi taxi **giúp tôi*** (could you call me a taxi). It's the gentlest way to ask for help — softer than *xin*, and much warmer.

grammars.title: Ordering: one frame for everything
body: Every row in this table uses the same pattern. Once you have it, you can order anything in Vietnam without pointing.
after: ⚠️ The fifth row is the emergency exit you must memorize: **Cho tôi một cái này** — "one of these, please" — while pointing. With that sentence alone you can eat anywhere in Vietnam from day one, without knowing a single dish name.
Adding *ạ* at the end raises the politeness by one notch and is always safe: *Cho tôi một bát phở ạ.* With a vendor much older than you, it's not optional but expected.

grammars.title: Hay or hoặc?
body: The one distinction in this unit that's truly new for English speakers. The rule is short and has no exceptions at A1.

rows: Monday or Tuesday, either is fine.

after: ⚠️ *Hay* has a second, completely different meaning: **"interesting, good"** — *Phim này hay quá!* ("this film is so good!"). Only position tells them apart: *hay* between two choices means "or"; *hay* after a noun means "good, interesting".
*Hay là* at the **start** of a sentence is a gentle way to suggest something — like English "how about…?". It's one of the most useful openers for inviting a friend.

blocks.text: ⚠️ *Thịt lợn* (pork) is used in the north, *thịt heo* in the south. If you don't eat pork, it's worth recognizing both — and the life-saving sentence is *Tôi không ăn thịt lợn.* or, safer still, *Tôi ăn chay.* ("I eat vegetarian"), understood everywhere because Buddhist meat-free days are very common in Vietnam.

Notice the building blocks again: *nước mắm* = water + salted fish, *bánh mì* = cake + wheat, *cà phê sữa* = coffee + milk, *thịt bò* = meat + cow. Vietnamese nouns can almost always be taken apart, and doing so is much cheaper than memorizing the whole sound.

sections.title: Flavors, and asking for what you want

blocks.title: Three table habits worth knowing
items: **All the dishes go in the middle and are shared**, while each person has their own rice bowl — unlike the Western one-plate-each style. Serving food to others — especially older people — is considered very polite.

**Before starting, the younger invite the older to eat**: *Cháu mời ông bà ăn cơm ạ.* or simply *Mời cả nhà ăn cơm.* Skipping it isn't fatal for a foreigner, but saying it will be noticed and appreciated.
**Never stand chopsticks upright in rice** — it looks like incense sticks on an ancestor altar, and that's a bad omen. Lay them across the bowl or on a chopstick rest.
Tôi ăn phở ____ bún đều được.
Thứ hai ____ thứ ba tôi rảnh.
Anh đi hôm nay ____ ngày mai?
